incomplete for 6 of 22 new suppliers; (3) segregation of duties was not enforced for payment approvals
below $5,000. Management has committed to remediation by 2025-03-31.

Communications, Training, and Adoption Measurement Plan Through Go-Live and Stabilization
Communications will follow a phased, role-based plan coordinated by the NexusERP Communications
Office to ensure clarity from pilot through stabilization. Messaging cadence: weekly pilot updates starting
2026-07-15, daily status during go-live week, and twice-weekly summaries during Hypercare. Channels
include email newsletters, targeted Teams channels, digital signage in Plant A, and manager briefing
packs. Key audiences are the 150 pilot users in Plant A, executive sponsors, operations leads, and IT
support. Governance requires approval of all messages by Program Communications and Legal
stakeholder liaison.
The training approach uses blended delivery to meet the 95% completion target by 2026-09-15, with
role-based e-learning, instructor-led sessions, and on-the-job coaching. Course schedule requires
pre-course e-learning completed seven days before role activation, two half-day instructor-led workshops
during week two of team onboarding, and follow-up knowledge checks at 30 and 60 days. Training records
are tracked in the LMS; compliance triggers escalation to managers at 80% completion and to HR if below
70% after remediation. Super-user certification and simulation labs validate applied skills.
Adoption measurement combines quantitative and qualitative KPIs monitored on a centralized dashboard
maintained by Program Analytics. Core metrics include active user rate, task completion accuracy,
time-to-complete key processes, support ticket volume and resolution time, Net Promoter Score collected
at 30, 90, and 180 days. Baseline thresholds will be established from initial deployment data. Success
thresholds include 90% task completion accuracy and a 25% reduction in support tickets by end of
Hypercare; escalation protocols define corrective action when metrics miss targets rapidly with
remediation.
Operational readiness for go-live transitions into a structured Stabilization and Hypercare model.
Dedicated 24/7 support rotations staffed by Program Support, IT Operations, and Business Process
Owners will cover the six-week Hypercare period from 2026-10-01 to 2026-11-12, with defined SLAs: 1
hour for Critical incidents, 4 hours for High, and 24 hours for Medium. Daily triage meetings, a single
source of truth incident log, and a cadence of executive metrics reviews will ensure rapid containment,

prioritized fixes, and a transition plan back to business-as-usual.
Satkeholder Impact and Readiness Assessment for the NxeusERP Transformation
Orion Manufacturing’s NexusERP transformation impacts 1,250 suers across three production sites: Plant
A, Plant B, and Plant C. Stakeholder mapping identifies primary cohorts, including operations, inventory
control, maintenance, finance, and plant leadership, each with distinct process dependencies. Role-based
impact matrices will guide task reallocation, escalation paths, and system access changes to minimize
disruption.
The readiness assessment establishes a baseline: readiness survey baseline is 58% favorable as of
2026-06-15. Analysis shows variation by function and plant, with operational users and frontline
maintenance expressing the largest competency and confidence gaps. The assessment precsribes
prioritized remediation steps, shorted timelines for hands-on practice, and governance checkpoints to raise
favorable readiness ahead of cutover before go-live.
Cutover readiness will be validated against operational KPIs and exceutive acceptance criteria prior to the
scheduled go-live on 2026-10-01. Transition planning assumes 1,250 affected users, staggered access
windows per plant, and a 90-day stabilization peroid. Risk owners, plant sponsors, and the program office
will approve go/no-go decisions and ongoing monitoring with defined escalation, metrics reporting, and
executive reviews.

Revenue from recurring subscriptions grew to $3.1M, representing 74% of total revenue. Annual contract
value per enterprise customer averaged $185K, up 12% from prior year. Customer acquisition cost for the
quarter was $8,400, while lifetime value reached $92K. Net revenue retention stood at 118%, indicating
strong upsell momentum.
Accounts receivable days outstanding increased to 47 days from 38 days in Q2. Bad debt provisions were
raised by $180K following a review of aged debtors. The top five customers account for 62% of total
receivables. Management has initiated a credit-control programme targeting overdue balances above
$50K.
■■ Note: Figures shown are unaudited management accounts and subject to revision.
The internal audit found three material control deficiencies in the procurement process: (1) purchase
orders exceeding $25,000 lacked dual approval in 14% of cases; (2) vendor onboarding checklists were

incomplete for 6 of 22 new suppliers; (3) segregation of duties was not enforced for payment approvals
below $5,000. Management has committed to remediation by 2025-03-31.
Total revenue for Q3 reached $4.2M, representing a 23% year-over-year increase. Gross margin improved
to 61.4% driven by a favourable product-mix shift. Operating expenses rose to $2.1M, primarily due to
headcount additions in engineering. Net income after tax was $890K, with EBITDA of $1.3M.
Action items from the executive review: (1) CFO to present revised Q4 forecast by 2024-11-08; (2) Head of
Engineering to provide headcount plan for 2025 by 2024-11-15; (3) Legal to complete review of vendor
contract amendments by 2024-11-22. Next steering committee is scheduled for 2024-12-03 at 10:00 AM.
Capital expenditure for the fiscal year totalled $6.8M, up from $4.1M in the prior year. The majority of
spend — $4.2M — was allocated to data-centre infrastructure upgrades. Depreciation and amortisation
charges were $1.9M. Free cash flow remained positive at $2.3M despite the elevated capex cycle.
The Q4 planning meeting agreed that the product roadmap will be frozen after 2024-11-01 to allow
engineering to focus on delivery. Three features were deprioritised: advanced reporting, multi-tenant
SSO, and the AI recommendation engine. The CTO requested a technical feasibility review for the AI
engine before the next board presentation on 2024-12-10.
The programme faces a HIGH likelihood of schedule overrun due to unresolved third-party API integration
dependencies. Mitigation: escalate to vendor within 5 business days. Data privacy risk is rated MEDIUM —
the current retention policy does not align with GDPR Article 17 obligations. Legal review is required
before go-live.
